<section id="about" class="intro-section" aria-labelledby="page-title">
      <div class="intro">
        <p class="eyebrow">University of Alberta · Department of Computing Science</p>
        <h1 id="page-title">U-A-Goose</h1>
        <p class="subtitle goose-acronym"><strong>G</strong>r<strong>O</strong>up <strong>O</strong>f <strong>S</strong>oftware <strong>E</strong>ngineering</p>
        <div class="research-text">
          <img class="goose" src="assets/images/coding_goose_1.png" alt="Our coding goose mascot" width="160" height="160">
          <p>We study <strong>trustworthy software engineering in the AI era</strong>, asking: <strong>How can we help AI learn from limited, incomplete experience to reliably build and evolve complex software systems?</strong></p>
          <p>We use software engineering knowledge to shape better learning objectives, experiences, and feedback, helping models explore beyond established solutions and refine their judgments in light of verifiable evidence.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

        <div class="pi-identity"><p class="eyebrow">Principal Investigator</p><h3>Prof. Zhou Yang</h3><p>Assistant Professor<br>University of Alberta<br>Canada CIFAR AI Chair<br>Amii Fellow</p><p class="person-links"><a href="https://homepage.zhouyang.me/">Homepage</a><a href="mailto:zy25@ualberta.ca">Email</a><a href="https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=4oWBhPsAAAAJ&amp;hl=en">Scholar</a></p></div>
        <div class="pi-bio"><p>Zhou Yang is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computing Science at the University of Alberta, a Canada CIFAR AI Chair, and an Amii Fellow. He completed his Ph.D. at Singapore Management University in early 2025, after earning an MSc from University College London. He previously served as a senior research engineer at the Centre for Research on Intelligent Software Engineering.</p>
<p>His research establishes scientific and practical foundations for trustworthy code LLMs, integrating robustness, security, privacy, ecosystem understanding, and efficiency to support safer AI adoption in software engineering. He has received multiple major awards, including the 2026 MSR Outstanding Doctoral Research Award, the 2025 ACM SIGSOFT Outstanding Doctoral Dissertation Award, and the 2024 IEEE Computer Society Best Paper Award.</p></div>
      </article>

    <section id="join" class="page-section" aria-labelledby="join-heading">
      <div class="section-heading"><h2 id="join-heading">Join the group</h2><a href="mailto:zy25@ualberta.ca">zy25@ualberta.ca <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></div>
      <p class="section-intro">We welcome self-motivated students interested in software engineering, trustworthy AI, and code LLM research.</p>
      <div class="openings-grid">
        <article><p class="eyebrow">Graduate study</p><h3>PhD / Master by Research</h3><p>Applications for <strong>Fall 2027 are now open</strong>, but <strong>only very limited positions are available</strong>.</p><p>Contact <a href="mailto:zy25@ualberta.ca">zy25@ualberta.ca</a> with your CV, transcript, and a brief description of your research interests.</p></article>
        <article><p class="eyebrow">Research experience</p><h3>Research assistants</h3><p>For current University of Alberta students, including ECE Master's students and undergraduates, interested in joining the group as research assistants.</p><p>Send your CV and transcript to <a href="mailto:zy25@ualberta.ca">zy25@ualberta.ca</a>.</p></article>
        <article><p class="eyebrow">Individual studies</p><h3>CMPUT 399 / CMPUT 499</h3><p>For University of Alberta undergraduates interested in taking an individual study course with the group.</p><p>Contact <a href="mailto:zy25@ualberta.ca">zy25@ualberta.ca</a> with your CV and transcript.</p></article>
      </div>
      <div class="screening">
        <div><h3>Getting started</h3><p>All prospective research assistants and individual study students go through a lightweight screening process, which typically involves:</p></div>
        <ol><li><span>01</span><div><h4>Read</h4><p>A few selected papers relevant to your intended research area.</p></div></li><li><span>02</span><div><h4>Present</h4><p>A short talk to demonstrate your understanding of the papers.</p></div></li><li><span>03</span><div><h4>Implement</h4><p>Reproduce or implement baseline methods.</p></div></li></ol>
        <p class="screening-note">We consider academic merits, prior research experience, and alignment with the group's research directions to assess research potential and ensure a good mutual fit.</p>
      </div>
    </section>
